prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [val][adversarial] Long group header over tiny sub-columns (language en).
Grid: 5 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Merged cells: "Model" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Benchmark accuracy on he" spans 3 col × 1 row; "Notes" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Model" · longest unbreakable word 45px · one-line width 45px
  col 2: header "Benchmark accuracy on held-out multilingual evaluation suite › EN" · longest unbreakable word 21px · one-line width 21px
  col 3: header "Benchmark accuracy on held-out multilingual evaluation suite › ZH" · longest unbreakable word 22px · one-line width 22px
  col 4: header "Benchmark accuracy on held-out multilingual evaluation suite › AR" · longest unbreakable word 21px · one-line width 21px
  col 5: header "Notes" · longest unbreakable word 63px · one-line width 581px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"Compare benchmark accuracy across three language evaluations for each model, alongside explanatory notes.","reading":"Readers scan down each language column to compare models and across each row to compare a model’s scores and note. Wrapped notes can increase row height, which can also accommodate wrapping elsewhere in the row.","groups":["EN, ZH, and AR are parallel accuracy measures under one shared benchmark heading and should have equal widths.","Model identifies each row; Notes supplies context for that row."],"keep_intact":["Model names","Language identifiers EN, ZH, and AR","Individual accuracy values","Words within the benchmark heading and notes"],"may_wrap":["The shared benchmark heading can wrap across multiple lines over the three language columns.","Notes can wrap naturally at word boundaries."]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[66,42,42,42,167],"idea":"Give notes the most room while keeping the three score columns equally narrow and their values intact."},{"name":"B","widths":[66,59,59,59,116],"idea":"Give the grouped benchmark heading and score columns more room, accepting more wrapping in notes."},{"name":"C","widths":[76,45,45,45,148],"idea":"Give model names breathing room and balance a moderately wide notes column against compact, equal score columns."}]}
